activity.title: Current request
activity.empty: Send a message to watch it travel through the pipeline.

chat.placeholder: Ask something. Lists and itemised tasks can be shared with the swarm.
chat.hint.team: A stored team runs this message as its plan. Privacy, role and passage rules still apply.
chat.partialTitle: Some steps could not be completed; the answer names them and why.
chat.attachHint: Text files up to 200 KB, read on this computer
chat.welcome: Your messages are answered by the models on this computer. With the swarm enabled, itemised requests are split into micro-tasks and shared with other Swarmbly computers.
chat.welcomeHint: Try: Extract one key fact per item from the following list of five items: apples, bridges, comets, drums, electrons. List 5 bullet points, one per item, separately.
chat.deleteBody: It is removed from this computer. Exports you saved are not affected.
chat.exportBody: Choose a format. The file stays on this computer.
chat.agreementTitle: Agreement between replicas is convergence, not correctness.

hint.local: Local: answered on this computer only.
hint.localMulti: Local with several models: itemised requests are spread across your local models; nothing leaves this computer.
hint.lan: Swarm LAN: itemised requests may be shared with authenticated computers on this network. Everything else is answered locally.
hint.auto: Automatic: Swarmbly shares a request only when it splits cleanly and workers are available.
hint.tierLocal: Your privacy tier is LOCAL, so nothing will be sent. Change it in Settings → Privacy to use the swarm.

chat.evidenceTitle: Public context from Wikipedia was added to {n} items; only those items' texts were sent.
chat.roleSourcesTitle: Results a circle member's public search or shared corpus returned. The requester cannot verify which engine answered.
chat.lceTitle: The answer used passages from your sources (LCE C1); they did not leave this device.
chat.publicOfferTitle: Your question is about you or your documents, so nothing public was looked up. If you accept, only these names are sent: {names}
chat.memorySavedTitle: Saved in {path}. On this computer only; used in the next answers.
chat.citeUnknownTitle: These labels match no passage or result given in this conversation: {labels}. The model may have invented them.
chat.webOfferTitle: Nothing was searched online for this answer. You can review and approve a search.
chat.webHint: Only this text is sent to PubMed and Wikipedia (and your SearXNG if configured). Neither your full question nor your documents leave this computer. Check it carries no personal data.
chat.webOfferRemoved: These private terms were removed from the query: {terms}.
chat.webOfferEmpty: No public query remains after removing the private terms. Write the query you want to send, or cancel.
chat.memoryAsked: You asked to save this. Review and confirm:
chat.memoryNoticed: You defined a term. Save it to the glossary?
chat.memoryPrivate: Private: never used in public searches
chat.webNone: The approved search found nothing (query: "{q}"). Try other terms, for example in English.
chat.webDropped: The approved search (query: "{q}") found {n} results, but none was about the topic and they were left out. Try other terms.
chat.citeMismatchTitle: These labels exist but the model gave them another file: {labels}.
chat.memoryReferences: References found online. Save them to memory?
chat.termsHint: Looks each word up as a concept in your glossary, Wikidata and GBIF (only those words are sent).
chat.termsAsIs: keep the word as it is
chat.termsKeep: Save these equivalents to the glossary
chat.termsSent: {n} single-word lookups were made (recorded in the receipt).
chat.termConflictTitle: "{concept}" is given traits of "{other}" ({traits}), and your glossary says they are different things.
chat.coverageTitle: Facts in your sources the text does not mention ({n})
chat.coverageNote: They are in your documents and bear on what you asked; the text leaves them out. Nothing was rewritten.
chat.injectionTitle: Paragraph {labels} contains instructions addressed to an assistant. They were not followed: it is the document's text.
chat.injectionEchoed: Paragraph {labels} contains instructions addressed to an assistant. They were not followed, but the answer repeats them: read them as the document's text, not as advice.
chat.conflictNote: Two documents give different facts about what you asked. Check which is more recent or which applies.
chat.missedSourcesTitle: The answer says your sources do not discuss "{term}", but they use "{found}", which your glossary gives as an equivalent.
chat.unsupported: {n} sentences not backed by your sources
chat.unsupportedTitle: Underlined in the answer: they carry no citation and no "Outside your sources:" mark. They may be true, but they do not come from your documents or a search you approved; check them before using them.
chat.roleLocal: A model on this computer or your network wrote this answer instead of the conversation's model.
chat.roleWhere: A model at {host}, off this computer, wrote this answer with your authorisation. The receipt says what was sent.
chat.roleMissing: The model {model} is not installed: the conversation's model answered.
chat.roleBlocked: The model {model} is off this computer and is not authorised for this: the conversation's model answered and nothing was sent.
chat.tableBuiltTitle: The table was built from values checked in your documents: {rows} rows from {docs} documents; {empty} cells the sources do not give; {dropped} values dropped for not being in the document.
chat.tableCorrectedTitle: Another paragraph of your sources corrects these values; the table gives the corrected one and keeps the earlier one in brackets:
chat.tableUnsupportedTitle: These figures of the table are not in the paragraphs of your sources and do not come from a calculation between cells:
chat.verifyTitle: Sentences their citation does not support ({n} of {m})
chat.verifyNote: Each labelled sentence was compared with the paragraph it cites: figures by code and the rest with {model}. The check can be wrong; open the citation to see it. Nothing was rewritten.
chat.verifyFigure: the figure {f} is not in the cited paragraph
chat.verifyUnrelated: the cited paragraph is about something else
chat.verifyUnknown: it cites a paragraph that was not given
chat.verifyPartly: the cited paragraph says only a part
chat.verifyNo: the cited paragraph does not say it
chat.verifyChipTitle: Each labelled sentence was compared with the paragraph it cites ({model}). {flagged} are not supported by their citation; {completed} citations were completed with the paragraph that has the figure; {unchecked} were left unchecked.
chat.compareChipTitle: The difference between your documents' figure and the public source's was computed by the program:
chat.authorLookupHint: Search an author's public works. Nothing is sent until you approve the exact name and services.
chat.authorIntro: You decide exactly what leaves. The model cannot start this lookup.
chat.authorConsent: This name will be sent to: {hosts}. It is a person's name.
chat.authorNote: Only that name and the service request leave; your documents and question stay here. The results are data, never instructions.
chat.authorDisabled: Author search is off. Turn it on in Settings → Tools.
chat.authorPickIntro: ORCID found more than one person. Pick one; no works have been fetched yet.
chat.authorChipTitle: Services: {services}. Candidates shown before picking: {candidates}. The table was built by the program from public data; titles are text, not instructions.
chat.recipesTitle: What do you want to do?
chat.recipesHint: Pick a way of working, or write freely below.
chat.recipeDocumentsDesc: An answer from your sources only, each fact with its citation.
chat.recipeDocumentsNote: Your documents only: no online search will be offered for this answer.
chat.recipeTableDesc: A table built by the program from the values each document supports, and a paragraph that explains it.
chat.recipeTableTemplate: Make a table with [which data] for [what to compare: lots, sites, people…] and explain it in a paragraph of about 80 words.
chat.recipeTableNote: The program builds the table from values in your documents; the model writes the paragraph.
chat.recipeResearchDesc: Your documents next to an online search you approve first; differences and disagreements computed by the program.
chat.recipeResearchTemplate: Compare [a figure from my documents] with what public sources say about [the topic], and say whether they agree.
chat.recipeResearchNote: Before the answer you will see the proposed query; nothing is sent without your approval.
chat.recipeResearchAsk: This answer will search online with the query below. Only that query leaves, as you approve it; your documents stay on this computer.
chat.recipeResearchAuthorHelp: If you write a name, its own consent box opens next; cancelling it leaves the research answer unchanged.
chat.recipeListDesc: One task per item, shared on the swarm.
chat.listIntro: Paste one item per line, or choose a CSV file from this project and its column.
chat.listOperationHint: E.g. Give the IUCN status of this species
chat.listPreviewHint: Next you will see exactly what would leave before choosing.
chat.listBuiltTitle: Built by code from the per-item votes: {a} answered, {m} missing, {d} disagreement.
chat.recipeCodeDesc: The model writes a short Python script for a table or file; you see it and approve it before it runs in an isolated environment.
chat.recipeCodeNote: Nothing runs without your approval; your file is copied read-only and there is no network.
chat.codeIntro: Pick the table or file the script will see. The model receives only the column headers and up to five rows.
chat.codeQuestion: What do you want to compute?
chat.codeNoSources: This project has no source files to use.
chat.codeSampleHint: The model never receives the whole file; the script reads it in an isolated environment.
chat.codeProposalIntro: The model wrote this script. Nothing has run yet. You can run it or cancel.
chat.codeLimitsText: Limits: {time} s, {memory} MiB of memory, {output} MiB of output per stream, {disk} MiB in /out.
chat.codeWatchdog: On Windows the disk limit is enforced by a watchdog only, not by the kernel (R-006).
chat.codeApproveHint: Running uses a single-use approval token; there is no automatic run.
chat.codeUnavailable: The isolated Python environment is not installed.
chat.codeUnavailableHint: Recipe 5 is unavailable until the optional sandbox extra is installed; nothing else is offered.
chat.codePreparing: The isolated environment is being prepared in the background.
chat.codeNotPrepared: The isolated environment has not been prepared yet.
chat.codeNotPreparedHint: Prepare it once from the sandbox notice or Settings → System (or run swarmbly-app --prepare-sandbox); this request runs without the code recipe.
chat.codePreparingHint: This request runs without the code recipe. You can keep chatting; try the recipe again when the sandbox notice says it is ready.
chat.codeLowMemory: There is not enough free memory to prepare the isolated environment safely.
chat.codeLowMemoryHint: The code recipe stays unavailable; this request runs without it. Close other applications or use a machine with more free memory, then try again from Settings.
chat.codePrepareFailed: The isolated environment could not be prepared.
chat.codePrepareFailedHint: Retry from Settings → System; this request runs without the code recipe.
chat.recipeFill: Fill in the parts in brackets before sending.
chat.recipeChipTitle: The answer was made with this recipe.
chat.useToolsHint: The model may propose an MCP tool call. You see the tool and its exact arguments before anything runs; only local MCP tools can be set to don't ask again in this project.
chat.useToolsUnavailable: The tools agent is not available. Install the optional agent extra to use MCP tools in a conversation.
chat.agentChipTitle: The answer records every call the model proposed and how it was decided.
chat.agentApprovalBody: Nothing has run yet. Check the tool, where it goes and the exact arguments.
chat.agentLocalNote: on this computer, with your rights
chat.agentRemember: Don't ask again in this project (local MCP tool only)

explore.title: How this answer was made

caveat.verification: Signatures were verified; layer-1 commitments do not exist yet in the protocol and were not simulated.
caveat.agreement: Agreement between models is convergence, not truth: models of different families share errors.
caveat.thresholds: Seam and agreement thresholds are placeholders until calibrated.

explore.agreementNote: Each unit shows how much the replicas agreed. HIGH means they converged; it does not mean the content is correct.
explore.evidenceNote: Public context (Wikidata, Wikipedia CC BY-SA 4.0, PubMed…) added. Only these names were sent:
explore.lceNote: Passages from your sources used in this answer (they did not leave this device):

receipt.title: What left this computer
receipt.nothing: Nothing left this computer for this answer.

kind.parte_consulta: part of the text you approved

receipt.consentNo: needed and not given: nothing was looked up

explore.citeTitle: Stable citation: the file's hash and the paragraph. It still holds if the project is moved or restored on another computer.

anchor.title: Anchoring to sources
anchor.note: A simple measure: it counts sentences carrying a label; it does not check that the label supports the sentence (that is 3.2's verifier).

agent.title: Tools in this answer
agent.none: No tool call was approved in this answer.

monitor.title: Swarm
monitor.lede: Computers running Swarmbly on your network. A node counts as authenticated once its identity is proven; announcements are not trusted until then.
monitor.nodeRolesNote: What this computer offers the swarm as a worker. A node role is placement information only: it never widens circle admission, egress or any other permission.
monitor.graphLabel: Map of this node and its peers
monitor.graphEmpty: No peers yet. Turn on the local network or connect by address.
monitor.discoveryNote: Each entry records when it was first seen, when an mDNS answer last confirmed it, and when it expires. Entries only refresh when a real answer arrives.
monitor.contributionNote: Work this computer did for others. Your own requests are not counted here.
monitor.lanRefused: You refused local network access. Change it in Settings → Permissions.
monitor.searchOff: Turn on the local network first
monitor.connectBody: Use this when your network blocks discovery. The other computer must run Swarmbly; its identity is verified before anything is exchanged.
monitor.diversityCaveat: More families reduce correlated errors but do not remove them.
monitor.cacheEmpty: Nothing discovered yet. Try Search now.

memory.title: Memory
memory.lede: The Local Cognitive Extension keeps a personal memory on this computer. It is optional and never changes how this computer serves others.
memory.docBody: Your documents stay in a local folder. Answers retrieve from them and the wiki records where every claim came from, so a source can be forgotten completely.
memory.behaviourBody: Style, terminology and procedures can shape requests through a small projection (at most 1 KB) added to the shared contract. Personal fine-tuning (C4) is experimental and off.
memory.notInVersion: Not available in this version of the app.
memory.sourcesBody: Put documents you want Swarmbly to remember in this folder. They are read, never modified.
memory.sourcesOff: Turn memory on to use a source folder.
memory.otherFoldersBody: Folders on this computer that are also read, without copying or changing them (your work documents, for example).
memory.c1Ready: Formats: text, Markdown, Word (.docx), HTML and PDF (with pdftotext). Passages are only used in answers made on this computer and never leave it; a glossary.md file ("term = equivalents") helps across languages.

settings.title: Settings
settings.lede: Every value can be changed and reverted. Defaults favour privacy: nothing is shared until you decide.
settings.moreInAdvanced: More parameters appear with the Advanced profile.

secretStored.file: stored in a protected file on this computer

tier.GLOBAL: GLOBAL: authenticated peers may receive fragments

reduce_motion.label: Reduce motion
reduce_motion.help: Turns off pulses and blinking. Your system preference is also respected.

output_dir.label: Output folder
output_dir.help: Where exports and saved reports go. Empty uses the output folder inside your Swarmbly data folder.

model__backend.label: Model runner
model__backend.help: Ollama is recommended. Any OpenAI-compatible server (llama.cpp, vLLM) or Anthropic's API also works.

model__backend_url.label: Runner address
model__backend_url.help: Leave empty for Ollama on this computer. For Anthropic, empty uses https://api.anthropic.com.

model__api_key.label: API key
model__api_key.help: Only for servers that ask for one, including Anthropic. Stored in the system keychain (or a protected file when there is none), never in the configuration.

model__model_name.label: Chat model
model__model_name.help: Answers locally, plans and assembles shared answers.

model__multi_model.label: Use several local models
model__multi_model.help: Spread work across local models of different families, and compare their answers when you ask for more than one response.

model__local_models.label: Local models to use
model__local_models.help: Pick at least two of different families.

model__local_parallel.label: Local models at once
model__local_parallel.help: How many local models may generate at the same time. More needs more memory.

model__temperature.label: Temperature
model__temperature.help: Lower is more focused; higher is more varied.

model__max_tokens_per_fragment.label: Fragment length limit
model__max_tokens_per_fragment.help: Maximum tokens each micro-task may produce.

model__embedder.label: Similarity
model__embedder.help: How seams and agreement are measured. Embeddings need an embedding model such as nomic-embed-text.

model__embed_model.label: Embedding model
model__embed_model.help: Name of the embedding model in Ollama.

swarm__lan_enabled.label: Local network
swarm__lan_enabled.help: Announce this computer and find others on this network (mDNS). Nothing is shared without a matching privacy tier.

swarm__k_min.label: Minimum responses per micro-task
swarm__k_min.help: Replicas sent from the start. Two or more give a map of where models disagree, at a proportional cost.

swarm__k_max.label: Maximum responses per micro-task
swarm__k_max.help: Ceiling including extra attempts for slow or failed workers.

swarm__n_fragments_max.label: Maximum fragments
swarm__n_fragments_max.help: Upper bound. The real number comes from the request's structure and the swarm's capacity.

swarm__max_concurrency.label: Micro-tasks in flight
swarm__max_concurrency.help: How many micro-tasks this computer keeps in the swarm at once.

swarm__timeout_ms.label: Micro-task timeout (ms)
swarm__timeout_ms.help: After this, the attempt counts as slow and another worker may be tried.

swarm__worker_enabled.label: Share this computer
swarm__worker_enabled.help: Serve micro-tasks for others with your base models. Your memory and files are never used.

swarm__worker_paused.label: Pause sharing
swarm__worker_paused.help: Keeps the connection but refuses new tasks.

swarm__worker_max_concurrent.label: Tasks at once
swarm__worker_max_concurrent.help: How many micro-tasks you serve simultaneously.

swarm__worker_only_idle.label: Only when idle
swarm__worker_only_idle.help: Refuse tasks while the processor is busy (heuristic).

swarm__worker_only_plugged.label: Only when plugged in
swarm__worker_only_plugged.help: On laptops, refuse tasks on battery.

swarm__hedge_fallback_ms.label: Extra attempt after (ms)
swarm__hedge_fallback_ms.help: Used until enough timings exist; then the observed 95th percentile is used.

swarm__tau_sem.label: Seam threshold τ
swarm__tau_sem.help: Placeholder until calibrated. Below it, a bridge sentence is written.

swarm__discovery_ttl_s.label: Discovery cache lifetime (s)
swarm__discovery_ttl_s.help: Entries without a fresh mDNS answer expire after this.

swarm__p2p_port.label: Swarm port (TCP)
swarm__p2p_port.help: Takes effect after restarting the app. Allow it in your firewall.

privacy__tier.label: Privacy tier
privacy__tier.help: Who may receive fragments of your requests. Requests are always classified on this computer first and can only be made stricter automatically.

privacy__trusted_networks.label: Trusted networks
privacy__trusted_networks.help: Informational only. Being on the same network never implies trust.

results__report_detail.label: Report detail
results__report_detail.help: Minimal reports leave out the text of requests and answers, so they can be shared safely.

results__auto_report.label: Save a report for every shared request

results__keep_stats.label: Keep statistics
results__keep_stats.help: Daily counters for the Swarm view.

evidence__enabled.label: Add public evidence
evidence__enabled.help: In lists of items that name something ("Blue-footed booby", "Ecuador") and in answers on this device that ask for current facts, the app looks the names up in public sources (Wikidata, Wikipedia, PubMed and, if installed, SearXNG) and adds the sentence with the fact. Only item names are sent, never your request or your documents, and nothing if the request is classified as sensitive. It is on by default: in tests it fixed what the models did not know (IUCN status 8/8, event years 5/5) without worsening what they already got right. You can turn it off here.

evidence__timeout_s.label: Maximum time per lookup (s)
evidence__timeout_s.help: If Wikipedia does not answer in time, the item is sent without evidence.

evidence__max_chars.label: Maximum characters per evidence
evidence__max_chars.help: The first two sentences of the entry are cut to this length.

evidence__local_answers.label: Also in answers made on this device
evidence__local_answers.help: When the answer is generated on this device (with your local sources), the app may look up to three names in public sources (Wikidata, Wikipedia, PubMed and, if installed, SearXNG): species, places or programmes your question names, or scientific names found in your sources. Only those names are sent (they are listed in "Explore processing"), never your question or your documents. The answer tells your sources [1] apart from public evidence [W1] and gives both when they differ. Requires public evidence to be on.

evidence__local_max_entities.label: Names looked up per local answer
evidence__local_max_entities.help: Maximum names sent to Wikipedia per answer generated on this device.

evidence__fusion_model.label: Model for answers with evidence
evidence__fusion_model.help: When an answer made on this device combines your local sources with public evidence, a larger local model can write it (slower, better attribution). Other answers keep the conversation's model.

evidence__providers.label: Public sources
evidence__providers.help: One per line, in order of trust: wikidata (structured facts: IUCN status, dates), wikipedia, pubmed (NCBI abstracts of scientific papers) and web (your SearXNG or Google, if you set the URL or the key below). Only names are sent to any of them, never your question or your documents.

evidence__searxng_url.label: Your SearXNG URL
evidence__searxng_url.help: Filled in by the installer below (Install and enable SearXNG). You can also enter the URL of your own SearXNG with JSON output enabled. Needs "web" in the sources.

evidence__google_cse_key.label: Google Custom Search key
evidence__google_cse_key.help: Only if you already had a Google Custom Search JSON API key: the API is closed to new customers and stops working on 1 January 2027. Also needs the search engine identifier and "web" in the sources.

evidence__google_cse_cx.label: Google engine id
evidence__google_cse_cx.help: The "cx" of your Programmable Search Engine.

privacy__third_party_models.label: Authorised third-party model services
privacy__third_party_models.help: A server outside this computer and your network belongs to another organisation. Swarmbly sends it nothing unless you write its address here (one per line). Every answer shows what was sent to it.

privacy__third_party_passages.label: Allow sending passages of my documents to those services
privacy__third_party_passages.help: Off: the service only gets your question and answers without your documents. Turn it on only if you accept that organisation receiving parts of your files.

roles__writer__model.label: Writer model
roles__writer__model.help: Writes compositions (reports, summaries, tables) from your sources. A larger model leaves out fewer facts and takes longer; questions stay with the conversation's model. Empty: the conversation's model.

roles__writer__think.label: Writer's reasoning
roles__writer__think.help: Some models reason before answering and spend the answer's room on it. "No" turns it off for the writer; "Model default" leaves the model as it is.

roles__search_terms__model.label: Model for search terms
roles__search_terms__model.help: Writes the terms your documents are searched with. Empty: the default model; in a composition, the writer if there is one.

roles__fusion__model.label: Model for answers with public evidence
roles__fusion__model.help: Writes the answers that join your sources with public evidence. Empty: the conversation's model.

roles__embeddings__model.label: Embedding model
roles__embeddings__model.help: Computes the vectors retrieval uses to find paragraphs of your documents. Empty: the app's current embedder (model.embed_model). Changing it rebuilds the project's index; vectors from two models are never mixed.

roles__embeddings__backend.label: Embeddings server
roles__embeddings__backend.help: Where embedding calls run. Anthropic has no embeddings endpoint, so it is not offered here. A server outside your network needs its host authorised and passages allowed; otherwise the app refuses before sending and falls back to the local embedder or to keyword search.

roles__embeddings__backend_url.label: Address of the embeddings server
roles__embeddings__backend_url.help: Ollama: http://127.0.0.1:11434. OpenAI-compatible: http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 (or just the host, and /v1 is added).

roles__embeddings__api_key.label: Key of the embeddings server
roles__embeddings__api_key.help: Kept in the system keychain, not in the configuration file.

roles__writer__backend.label: Writer's server
roles__writer__backend.help: By default the writer uses the conversation's server. Another server follows the same policy as any model: outside your network it receives nothing unless you authorise it, and your documents only with the second authorisation.

roles__writer__api_key.label: Key of the writer's server
roles__writer__api_key.help: Kept in the system keychain, not in the configuration file.

node_roles__large_model_min_b.label: Large-model threshold (B)
node_roles__large_model_min_b.help: Shared models at or above this parameter count are announced as large_model; 7 B is the default because it is the smallest widely available class clearly above the 1–3 B models this swarm mostly runs.

node_roles__reasoner_models.label: Reasoning models
node_roles__reasoner_models.help: Shared models you mark here are announced as reasoner and used with think: true. Empty by default.

node_roles__search__enabled.label: Share public search
node_roles__search__enabled.help: When on, this worker runs a public query for a member of a trusted circle on that member's behalf; only the query leaves this computer, never your files or conversation.

node_roles__corpus__project_id.label: Corpus to share
node_roles__corpus__project_id.help: One local project. Only admitted peers in the circles you select see its display name and size bucket, never titles, paths or contents.

node_roles__corpus__display_name.label: Corpus display name
node_roles__corpus__display_name.help: The name admitted peers see. Keep it free of personal details; at most 40 characters.

circle__admission_mode.label: Peer admission
circle__admission_mode.help: Only my circles requires a valid signed manifest that lists both nodes. My own devices keeps the 3.4 LAN behaviour (any authenticated peer on the LAN).

circle__node_name.label: Circle display name
circle__node_name.help: The name this node shows in manifests and invitations. Empty uses the computer name.

models.noLicence: Ollama did not report a licence for this model.
models.downloadNote: Models are downloaded by Ollama after you confirm. Suggestions fit this computer's memory.
models.consentBody: Ollama will download this model to this computer.
models.sizeUnknown: reported by Ollama when it starts
models.checkedOn: Size and licence checked on {date}; the licence Ollama reports after downloading is the one that applies.
models.downloadsRefused: Model downloads are off. Change it in Settings → Permissions.

privacy.identityBody: This Ed25519 public key identifies this computer in the swarm. The private key never leaves this computer.
privacy.lanNotTrust: Being on the same network is not trust: every peer proves its identity, and workers never receive the session or your whole request.

lan_discovery.label: Find other Swarmbly computers on this network
lan_discovery.help: Announces this computer with mDNS and listens for others. No other devices are scanned.

model_downloads.label: Allow model downloads through Ollama
model_downloads.help: You still confirm each download after seeing its size and licence.

internet.label: Join swarms over the internet
internet.help: Arrives in Phase 3 with rendezvous servers.

rec.reversible: Applying saves your current settings first. Sharing and the local network are never turned on by a recommendation.

sandbox.noticeBody: The code recipe needs a WebAssembly Python that compiles once on this computer: about {time} s and {memory} GB of memory. Preparing it now runs in the background and the chat stays usable.
sandbox.expected: Expected: {time} s and {memory} GB; {free} GB free now (at least {min} GB needed).
sandbox.free: Only {free} GB of memory are free; at least {min} GB are needed to start safely.
sandbox.forceWarning: The compile may take minutes and slow this computer or swap. Close other apps first.
sandbox.forcingToast: Preparing anyway; the computer may be slow until it finishes.
sandbox.preparingToast: Preparing the isolated environment in the background.
sandbox.failedToast: The isolated environment could not be prepared; see the notice.
sandbox.preparing: Preparing the isolated environment ({stage}). You can keep chatting; the code recipe waits until it is ready.
sandbox.ready: The isolated environment is ready: compiled in {time} s, peak {peak} MiB.
sandbox.notInstalled: The optional sandbox extra is not installed; the code recipe is unavailable. Install it with pip install 'swarmbly-app[sandbox]'.
sandbox.settingsBody: The first code recipe compiles WebAssembly Python once, then reuses the cache. Prepare it from here if you skipped the first-launch notice.

doctorExport.title: Doctor export
doctorExport.body: Writes one JSON and one readable text file to attach to a bug report. It contains only App/LCE/Core versions, OS and architecture, Python, CPU/RAM/GPU class, installed extras, whether Ollama answers and its model tags, the sandbox state and compile measurements, P2P counts and relay/push codes, and the last error codes with timestamps.
doctorExport.never: It never contains node ids or keys, names, circle names or ids, member names, IP addresses or host names, paths under your home, project names, document titles, prompts, answers, glossary, memory, API keys or the relay host.
doctorExport.previewTitle: Doctor export: what will be saved

doctor.ollamaPurpose: runs the models on this computer

state.pin_mismatch: differs from the pinned version ({pin}); "Install" updates it

doctor.installBody: They are installed into Swarmbly's own environment with pip. Your system Python is not changed.
doctor.installing: Installing… this can take a few minutes.
doctor.manual: Run this in a terminal (Swarmbly never changes the system Python):
doctor.firewall: If other computers cannot find this one, allow the swarm port (TCP) and mDNS (UDP 5353) in your firewall.

wizard.title: Set up Swarmbly
wizard.welcomeTitle: Your computer, part of a swarm
wizard.welcomeBody: Swarmbly answers with the models on your computer. When you allow it, it splits itemised requests into small tasks that other Swarmbly computers solve in parallel, then assembles the answer here.
wizard.welcomePrivacy: Nothing leaves this computer until you choose a privacy tier that allows it.
wizard.systemBody: Swarmbly needs a few Python packages and a model runner (Ollama).
wizard.profileBody: Based on what was measured. Each value says why; you can change any of them later.
wizard.modelsBody: Models run inside Ollama. Downloads only happen when you confirm them.
wizard.downloadLater: Downloads continue in the background; you can also download later in Settings → Models.
wizard.permBody: Choose what Swarmbly may do on your network. You can change these any time.
wizard.permLater: Allowing the local network does not share anything by itself: sharing also requires a privacy tier and, for others to use this computer, turning on sharing.
wizard.memoryBody: Optional personal memory that stays on this computer.
wizard.memoryLater: More levels are described in Memory.
wizard.doneBody: Swarmbly is set up. The Swarm view shows other computers as they appear, and every answer can be explored step by step.
wizard.answerBoth: Choose Allow or Not now for each question to continue.

websearch.title: Web search (optional)
websearch.body: A free metasearch engine (SearXNG) installed on this computer can query DuckDuckGo, Google, Google Scholar, Bing, Brave, PubMed, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex and Crossref without API keys. It listens on this computer only (127.0.0.1) and starts and stops with the app.
websearch.webOff: "web" is not in Public sources: add it to use this search.
websearch.started: Installing SearXNG; this can take a few minutes
websearch.ready: SearXNG installed and running; "web" was added to public sources
websearch.failed: SearXNG could not be installed; see the details in Settings → Privacy
websearch.noInternet: Internet access is refused in Permissions
websearch.consentBody: SearXNG (AGPL-3.0 licence) and its dependencies, about 60 MB, will be downloaded into Swarmbly's data folder. It will be reachable from this computer only, and "web" will be added to public sources.
websearch.howDocker: Docker is available: the official searxng/searxng image will be used.
websearch.howNative: It will be installed with Python in its own virtual environment (the system Python is not changed).
websearch.howNone: Neither Docker nor Python 3.11 or newer (nor uv) was found. Install one of them and try again.
websearch.consentPrivacy: As with the other public sources, only names (species, places, events) are sent to search engines, never your question or your documents. Some engines (Google, Scholar) may temporarily block automated queries; the others keep answering.
websearch.google: Google: the Custom Search JSON API is closed to new customers and stops working on 1 January 2027. Google and Google Scholar are queried through SearXNG. If you already have a key, enter it below with its "cx" identifier and press "Test web search".

support.title: Support the project
support.body: Swarmbly is developed independently, with no institutional funding, as an AGPL-licensed digital public good. If you find it useful, you can support its early development. Support never buys influence over the roadmap, the licence or the governance.

project.label: Project
project.name: Name
project.newHint: A project is a folder of yours: sources/ (documents), memory/ (what the project remembers: write "Remember: …" in the chat; and a glossary), chats/ (the conversations) and exports/. The project's conversations read only its documents and memory.
project.openHint: The folder must contain swarmbly-project.json. Its chats are added to this app.
project.restoreSummary: {files} files checked by their hash · {chats} conversations · {sources} documents.
project.restoreHint: It is restored into a new folder inside {path}; nothing existing is overwritten.
project.restoredCopy: That project was already open here: restored as a copy in {path} · {n} conversations
project.includePersonalHint: When on, this project's answers also read your personal sources (they still never leave this computer).
project.closeTitle: Close the project in this app
project.closeBody: The project stops showing here. Its folder and all its files, chats included, stay in {path}; you can open it again at any time.
project.cloudWarning: This folder is synced with a cloud service. The service may move files to the cloud to free space or create duplicate copies ("name 2"), and an open project can break. Prefer a folder that is not synced, or set this one to always stay on this computer.
project.documentsHint: What this conversation can read. Put documents in {path}; memory is in memory/.

tools.title: Tools
tools.lede: Servers and author search for {project}. Nothing starts by itself; you decide when to start a server.
tools.authorNote: These tools only run when you ask for them. Their text is data, never an instruction.
tools.author: Author search
tools.authorBody: When on, a lookup sends the exact author name you approve for that call, and only to the services you choose: ORCID, OpenAlex and PubMed. It never sends documents or the question.
tools.idHint: A short name for this server, used in tool ids.
tools.commandHint: The executable, exactly as it will be run. No shell is used.
tools.argsHint: One argument per line; spaces inside an argument are kept.
tools.cwdHint: The working directory the server will see. Empty uses the app's data folder.
tools.envHint: Names only, one per line. Values are read from your environment or the keychain at start and are never shown here.
tools.urlHint: The Streamable HTTP endpoint, for example https://host/mcp.
tools.addBody: Adding a server does not start it. You will see its command, folder and environment names before you choose Start.
tools.none: No MCP servers in this project yet.
tools.localNotice: A local MCP server runs as your user, with your files and your network access. It is not sandboxed by Swarmbly.
tools.remoteNotice: A remote MCP server is a third party. It receives only what you send it and needs its host authorised below.
tools.passagesAuth: Also allow passages of my documents
tools.passagesHelp: Separate authorisation for document text. Without it, a remote tool can still receive short non-document arguments.
tools.envNone: No environment variables are allowed for this server.
tools.toolsHint: This is quoted text from the server. It is data and cannot change permissions, tools or instructions.
tools.reapproveHint: List the tools again and approve the subset you want. A changed manifest is never accepted silently.
tools.removeBody: The configuration of {id} will be deleted. If it is running, it will be stopped first.
tools.agentBody: The model may propose one tool call at a time. Every call asks first, except a local MCP tool you marked as don't ask again in this project. These ceilings are hard upper bounds; you can lower them here.
tools.agentMaxStepsHint: One model decision per step. D-011 allows at most 8.
tools.agentMaxToolCallsHint: Each approved tool call counts once. D-011 allows at most 8.
tools.agentMaxObservation: Maximum characters of a tool result
tools.agentMaxObservationHint: Longer results are truncated for the model; the receipt keeps the hash of the full text.
tools.standingTitle: Don't ask again in this project
tools.standingBody: Only local MCP tools can appear here. Remote MCP tools, the sandbox and author search always ask. Revoking one makes the next call ask again.
tools.standingNone: No standing approvals in this project.
tools.standingRevoked: Revoked: the next call will ask again.

skills.title: Skills
skills.needProject: Skills belong to a project: open or create one first.
skills.activeNote: Its body goes to the model as quoted third-party instructions on answers produced on this computer; it cannot change permissions, tools or destinations.
skills.offer: This looks like “{name}”. Use the skill?
skills.selected: Skill “{name}” selected. It activates only for your next messages; nothing runs by itself.
skills.notGranted: requested by the skill — not granted
skills.nothingIgnored: No files were ignored on import.
skills.errors: Folders that could not be read · {n}
skills.importHelp: The app copies only SKILL.md and its .md/.txt references into this project's skills/ folder. Scripts, executables, binaries, archives and links are left out and listed here; nothing is run or imported as code.
skills.overwrite: Replace it if a skill with the same name exists
skills.usedTitle: The model saw this skill's body as quoted material (SHA-256 {sha}…).

circle.title: Trusted circles
circle.lede: A circle is a signed member list kept by its owner. Only nodes listed in a current, unexpired manifest can connect and be given tasks.
circle.none: No circles yet. Create one, or accept an invitation from another node.
circle.name: Circle name
circle.codeHelp: The code is signed by the owner. Accepting sends a signed join request; the owner still has to approve it.
circle.qr: Scan this QR with the other device, or send the code.
circle.leaveConfirm: Leave this circle? This device will no longer be admitted by its members.
circle.deleteConfirm: Delete this circle? Members will be told it was dissolved.
circle.noticeTitle: Your installation kept the 3.4 LAN admission
circle.noticeBody: This release adds trusted circles; new installations admit peers only through a circle manifest. Because this installation already existed, it keeps the old «my own devices» LAN admission until you choose. Review the choice in Settings → Swarm, or switch to circle-only now.
circle.stale: This node does not hold the current manifest; it will fetch it before being admitted.
circle.ownerOnly: Only the circle owner can do that.
circle.accepted: Join request sent. Waiting for the owner's approval.
circle.pending: Saved. It will be sent when the owner is reachable.
circle.passagesHelp: When on, recipe 4 may attach passages of your documents to items sent to members of this circle. Off by default; separate from privacy.third_party_passages.
circle.corpusShareHelp: This circle may retrieve passages from the shared corpus. Every admitted peer sees its display name and size bucket.
circle.corpusPickFirst: Choose a project in Settings → Swarm first.
circle.ownPassages: Document passages to my own devices
circle.ownPassagesHelp: When on, recipe 4 may attach passages of your documents to items sent to peers in my-own-devices mode. Off by default; separate from privacy.third_party_passages.
circle.relayHelp: The pin is mandatory. The owner pushes every new signed manifest version to the relay over a registered connection; the signed file in the operator spool is only the bootstrap copy and the fallback.
circle.relayPinRequired: A relay needs both an address and its certificate pin.
circle.relayNoneOwner: No relay for this circle. Set one to let members reach each other beyond the LAN.
circle.relaySecurity: SECURITY WARNING: certificate pin mismatch; this relay is stopped
circle.relayPushSource: The push is the primary path. The signed file in the operator's spool is the bootstrap copy and the fallback when the network push cannot run.
circle.relayPushUnknownCircle: the operator must install the first manifest for this circle on the relay
circle.relayPushRateLimited: the relay limits owner pushes to 30 per hour; the newest version stays queued
circle.relayPushStale: the relay already holds a newer version
circle.relayPushNotOwner: this node is not the relay's current owner
circle.relayPushOther: see the relay state and try again

teams.title: Teams
teams.lede: A team is a stored plan: named steps, each with an optional node role and dependencies on earlier steps. The same team runs on one computer (its local model pool) or across circle members, by role. A team never adds a permission.
teams.none: No teams yet. Create one or duplicate an example.
teams.loadFailed: The teams could not be read: {e}
teams.name: Name
teams.stepsRequired: Every step needs a name and an instruction.
teams.placeholderRequired: At least one step must contain {request}.
teams.requestHint: Use {request} where the user's message belongs. A step may depend only on earlier steps.
teams.duplicateHint: The copy is yours; the example stays read-only.
teams.deleteHint: This only removes the stored template; answers already made are not touched.
teams.picked: Team “{name}” will run the next message.

credits.title: Reciprocity credits
credits.lede: Credits are a courtesy inside a circle, not money. When you accept a verified result from a member, you sign a receipt for that member; they can offer it back just before sending you work, and it may let their task wait for a busy slot. A receipt belongs only to the worker it names, only in that circle, and expires. There is no transfer, sale, market or shared ledger: the balance is local, and a spend reported twice is flagged only at the issuer — detection, not prevention.
credits.empty: No circle yet. Credits are earned inside a trusted circle.
credits.flaggedHelp: The issuer logs what it issued and what workers reported spent. This is detection, not prevention, and nothing is broadcast beyond the circle.
credits.noFlagged: No receipt was reported spent twice.
